ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an inscribed triangle of circle $\odot O$ with $AB$ as the diameter. $BD$ is tangent to $\odot O$ at point $B$, and intersects the extension line of $AC$ at point $D$. $E$ is the midpoint of $BD$, and $CE$ intersects the extension line of $BA$ at point $F$. Given that $BD=8$, and $BE = \frac{1}{3}EF$. $FC$ is a tangent line of $\odot O$; find the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $BD=8$ and point $E$ is the midpoint of $BD$,\\
hence $BE= \frac{1}{2}BD=4$,\\
since $BE= \frac{1}{3}EF$,\\
thus $EF=3BE=12$,\\
in $\triangle FBE$, $BF= \sqrt{EF^{2}-BE^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}-4^{2}}=8\sqrt{2}$,\\
from (1) we have $\angle OCF=\angle ABD=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle F=\angle F$,\\
thus $\triangle FOC\sim \triangle FEB$,\\
hence $\frac{OC}{BE}=\frac{OF}{EF}$,\\
let $OC=x$, then $OF=BF-OB=8\sqrt{2}-x$,\\
hence $\frac{x}{4}=\frac{8\sqrt{2}-x}{12}$,\\
thus $x=2\sqrt{2}$,\\
hence $AF=8\sqrt{2}-2x=4\sqrt{2}$;\\
Therefore, the length of $AF$ is $\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle ⊙O; points A, B, C are on the circle; AB passes through the center O of the circle and is the diameter of the circle; B is at the upper right of the circle, A is near the lower left of the circle, and C is near the lower right of the circle. Draw tangent BD through B; point E is located on BD and between B and D. Point F is on the extension of BA; F, C, E are on the same straight line; from the figure it can also be seen that FC is the tangent to the circle at point C. Reasoning: Since BD=8 and E is the midpoint of BD, BE=BD/2=4. Also because BE=(1/3)EF, EF=3BE=12. Since BD is tangent to the circle at point B, and AB, that is, the line where OB lies, is perpendicular to tangent BD, FB⊥BE, and triangle FBE is right-angled at B. Therefore BF=sqrt(EF^2-BE^2)=sqrt(12^2-4^2)=sqrt(128)=8sqrt(2). Let the radius of the circle OC=OB=x. Since FC is tangent to the circle at point C, OC⊥FC; also BD is tangent to the circle at point B, so OB⊥BE. And F, O, B are collinear, F, C, E are collinear, so ∠OFC and ∠BFE are the same angle; therefore △FOC∼△FEB. According to the corresponding side ratio of similar triangles, OC/BE=OF/EF. Since OF=BF-OB=8sqrt(2)-x, x/4=(8sqrt(2)-x)/12. Solving gives 12x=32sqrt(2)-4x, 16x=32sqrt(2), x=2sqrt(2). Thus AB=2x=4sqrt(2), and F, A, B are collinear with A between F and B, so AF=BF-AB=8sqrt(2)-4sqrt(2)=4sqrt(2).
